# Provenance for the HasWorkingIndicator pane fixtures. Hand-captured from
# three LIVE codex sessions running under bossd (tmux capture-pane -p | tail
# -30), not generated by a script: the background-work footer only renders
# while a real background terminal is alive, so there is no way to fake the
# state that matters without a genuine long-running child.
#
# The three panes are a discriminating set — they differ ONLY in the signal
# under test, which is what makes the control meaningful:
#
#   working_background_terminal.txt
#       Turn ENDED ("Worked for 25m 25s"), composer available, one background
#       terminal still alive. This is the reported bug: codex answered
#       HasWorkingIndicator false, the pane stopped changing, and the poller
#       flipped a chat with live background work to IDLE after 5s.
#
#   working_spinner_background_terminals.txt
#       Turn LIVE. Codex appends the background-work footer to the spinner
#       line itself ("• Working (34m 54s • esc to interrupt) · 1 background
#       terminal running · …"), which is the evidence that this footer is
#       composer CHROME redrawn every frame, not frozen transcript text — so
#       it needs no staleness check, unlike claude's lingering completed-turn
#       summary. The 34m elapsed also pins the minute-scale spinner grammar
#       that the old codexWorking regex could not match.
#
#   idle_no_background_work.txt
#       Turn ended, no background work, composer available. Genuinely IDLE.
#       Proves the footer is ABSENT when the state is false, i.e. the detector
#       keys on a real signal rather than on ordinary end-of-turn chrome.
#
codex-cli: gpt-5.6-terra (statusline-reported model)
tmux: 3.7b
pane: 220x58 (last 30 rendered lines kept)
os: darwin-arm64 (25.4.0)
captured: 2026-09-15
